w:r.w:t: During a security assessment of the MyCES-FMS (Facility Management System) infrastructure, the production backend API server was discovered to have a publicly accessible Swagger UI at the following URL:

The Swagger UI exposes the complete API documentation for the NestJS backend, revealing 1,705 API endpoints covering all modules of the system including authentication, user management, HR, finance, compliance, facility management, and more.
1,705 API endpoints fully documented and publicly accessible
7,740 user records leaked via an unauthenticated endpoint
83 file upload endpoints with no authentication guard
Administrator credentials discovered via weak password
Full system compromise possible with a single API call

The Swagger endpoint was discovered through source code analysis of the frontend application (FE_Web/src/boot/axios.js), which revealed the production API base URL as "https://aziz.myces-fms.com/". The NestJS source code in Aziz/nest-auth/src/main.ts confirmed the Swagger module is configured at the "/api" path.
Confidentiality: HIGH, Integrity: HIGH, Availability: HIGH

The Swagger UI is deployed to the production environment without any access control. It provides an interactive interface to explore and test all 1,705 API endpoints. An attacker can browse the entire API surface, understand request/response schemas, and execute API calls directly from the browser.
Facility Management (PPM, work orders, equipment, inventory)
Human Resource (Org charts, manpower, training, personnel)
File System (Upload, download, delete, directory scan)

The endpoint POST /noauth/findUser/withCondition accepts arbitrary query conditions and returns full user records without requiring any authentication. This endpoint is designed for public access (the "noauth" prefix) but leaks sensitive data.
id, name, IC, email, password hash, phone, designation, department, rate, OT rates, image_file, etc.

The Swagger specification declares ZERO security requirements for all 1,705 endpoints. While some endpoints have runtime guards (returning 403 when no valid session cookie is present), several critical endpoints are truly unprotected:
POST /noauth/findUser/withCondition — Query users with arbitrary conditions
GET /noauth/loginAduan/{IC} — Login using IC number only
Auth Endpoints Without Swagger Security Declaration

83 file upload endpoints were identified in the Swagger specification. These endpoints accept file uploads for various purposes including Excel imports, images, documents, and system files. Without proper authentication and file type validation, these endpoints are susceptible to malicious file uploads leading to Remote Code Execution (RCE).
POST /auth/excel — Excel upload for auth module
POST /news/uploadmulti — Multiple file upload for news

103 DELETE endpoints were identified. These allow deletion of critical business data including user records, reports, daily records, HR documents, compliance documents, vehicles, drivers, bins, and more. While some have runtime guards, the Swagger specification declares none.
Result: Full Swagger UI with 1,705 endpoints accessible without authentication.
Result: 7,740 user records returned including password hashes, IC numbers, emails, and phone numbers.
Result: Login successful as "admin" user type. Session cookie obtained.
After login, all API endpoints become accessible with the session cookie:
This grants full administrative access to the system.
Result: 631 KB Swagger JSON file downloaded containing the complete API specification.
• 7,740 user PII records exposed (names, IC numbers, emails, phones)
• 1,744 password hashes available for offline cracking
• Complete API documentation reveals all business logic and data structures
• Company structure, departments, roles, and permissions fully enumerated
• Ability to create, modify, or delete users, roles, and permissions
• Ability to upload arbitrary files to the server
• Ability to modify business-critical data (PPM, work orders, inventory, HR)
• 103 DELETE endpoints available for data destruction
• Mass deletion of records possible via DELETE endpoints
• File system operations can delete or corrupt files
• Potential for DoS through resource-intensive API calls
• Regulatory non-compliance (PDPA 2010 — Personal Data Protection Act Malaysia)
• Operational disruption if data is deleted or corrupted
DISABLE Swagger UI in production immediately. Add environment check in main.ts:
FIREWALL aziz.myces-fms.com to only allow whitelisted IP addresses
ROTATE all user passwords — 1,744 password hashes have been exposed
BLOCK the /noauth/findUser/withCondition endpoint or require authentication
Implement proper authentication guards on ALL API endpoints
Add @ApiBearerAuth() or @ApiCookieAuth() decorators to Swagger configuration
Conduct a full audit of file upload endpoints — implement file type validation, size limits, and malware scanning
Review all DELETE endpoints — ensure proper authorization checks
Implement rate limiting on all API endpoints
Enable proper CORS configuration with specific origins only
Add CSP headers to the API responses
Implement audit logging for all sensitive operations
Implement API gateway with authentication and authorization
Deploy Web Application Firewall (WAF) in front of the API
Set up monitoring and alerting for unusual API activity
Implement proper password policy (minimum complexity, rotation)
Data classification and PII handling policy review
